key_insight: A SCAPS-1D + machine-learning workflow can rapidly rank multilayer perovskite solar-cell designs and pinpoint material choices that maximize efficiency, including lead-free double perovskites.
engineering_relevance: The study provides a practical screening framework for optimizing ETL, absorber, and HTL combinations before expensive full-scale fabrication or simulation.
method: Simulated 125 ETL/absorber/HTL device architectures with SCAPS-1D.
Trained an ML model on a representative subset to predict PCE for unexplored stacks.
Used SHAP to identify the most influential descriptors and verify top candidates with full device simulations.
evidence_signal: Leave-One-Group-Out cross-validation showed strong ranking performance, and the best verified devices reached 28.85% PCE (FTO/TiO2/Cs2AgBiBr6/NiO/Ag) and 28.62% PCE (FTO/SnO2/Cs2AgInBr6/NiO/Ag).
watch_item: The rankings depend on the quality and coverage of the SCAPS-generated training space, so extrapolation to materially different device physics or unmodeled interfaces may be unreliable.
paper_title: Multilayer Screening of Double and Conventional Perovskite Solar Cells Using SCAPS-1D and Machine Learning: Optimization of ETL, HTL, and Absorber for High-Efficiency Architectures
